text: The pipeline begins with the input referring expression describing the target object attributes.
Simultaneously, the input query image containing multiple candidate objects is provided.
Both inputs are passed through the backbone and feature enhancer to extract cross-modal representations.
This produces multi-scale visual features across four pyramid levels.
The visual features are projected via a mapping layer into the text embedding space.
Meanwhile, the corresponding text feature representation is retrieved.
The specific referring expression feature is selected.
It is element-wise multiplied with the projected visual features.
This yields image-text similarity features highlighting regions matching the expression.
The similarity features and multi-scale visual features feed into the U-shaped contextual attribute density estimator.
The estimator predicts an attribute density map for the query.
The prediction is compared against the ground-truth density map.
A density loss supervises the estimator to learn accurate contextual attribute distributions.
Intermediate representations from the estimator form the multi-scale contextual attribute density features.
Next, the spatial attention branch of the attention module enhances foreground attribute regions.
The multi-scale density features enter spatial pooling.
Two-dimensional max pooling captures peak attribute activations across channels.
Average pooling extracts mean spatial activation statistics.
Both pooled maps are concatenated along the channel dimension.
A convolutional layer processes the merged spatial statistics.
A sigmoid function produces the spatial attention map.
Processing continues in the channel attention branch.
Visual features from the backbone enter this stage.
They are modulated by the spatial attention map.
One-dimensional max pooling summarizes channel-wise extremes across spatial locations.
One-dimensional average pooling captures overall channel distributions.
A shared multi-layer perceptron transforms the pooled descriptors.
The outputs are summed together.
A sigmoid activation computes the channel attention weights.
These weights scale the spatially attended visual features.
This produces the final contextual attribute density enhanced visual features.
In parallel, the dynamic query module initializes object queries.
Contextual attribute density features are passed into the density initialization branch.
The top-k locations with highest text similarity are extracted.
Within the text initialization branch, initial query content is formed.
The text features are extracted.
They pass through a linear layer and a non-linear activation.
Initial query embeddings are introduced.
Matrix multiplications compute dynamic text weighting over the word tokens.
A cross-attention layer fuses the text-initialized queries with the top-k density features.
This yields refined dynamic queries encoding both attribute semantics and visual density.
The enhanced visual features, text features, and dynamic queries are assembled.
They are fed into the cross-modal localization decoder.
The decoder outputs precise bounding box localizations for counting target objects.
Finally, the entire model is optimized end-to-end using a localization loss combined with the density loss.
